ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two side-by-side barrel-shaped containers, with horizontal bottoms and vertical side walls. In the placement method on the left, the large ball a is located at the upper left and contacts the left side wall, the small ball b is located at the lower right and contacts the bottom of the container, and the two balls contact each other. In the placement method on the right, the large ball a is located at the lower right and contacts the bottom of the container, the small ball b is located at the upper left and contacts the left side wall, and the two balls contact each other. The problem statement indicates that both balls are smooth metal balls, and ma>mb. Reasoning: Regard ball a and ball b as one whole system. The contact force between the two balls is an internal force of the system, and cancels out in the force analysis of the whole. Since all contacts are smooth, the elastic force of the vertical side wall on a ball is along the horizontal direction and provides no vertical component, so it does not affect the vertical equilibrium of the whole. Write the equilibrium equation in the vertical direction for the two balls as a whole: the downward external force is the total gravity (ma+mb)g, and the upward external force is the supporting force N of the bottom of the container on the ball. In static equilibrium, N=(ma+mb)g. In the two placement methods, the total mass of the two balls is the same, and the side wall still only provides a horizontal elastic force, so the magnitude of the bottom supporting force is the same; according to action and reaction, the magnitude of the elastic force of the ball on the bottom of the container is also the same.
